- [USER] User expressed interest in the Cherry Blossom Festival in Japan.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Cherry Blossom Festival in Japan, also known as Hanami, is a traditional Japanese custom where people gather outdoors to view the blooming of cherry blossom trees (Sakura).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The festival takes place every spring, typically from late March to mid-April, depending on the location.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Cherry Blossom Festival is significant in Japanese culture as it signifies the arrival of spring and new beginnings.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The festival is celebrated to mark the fleeting nature of life, as the cherry blossom lasts for only a few weeks before falling from the trees.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Popular locations for viewing Cherry Blossom include Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka, Hiroshima, and Hokkaido.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] During the festival, people gather in parks, temples, and other outdoor areas with friends and family to enjoy the view of the cherry blossoms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Many people picnic under the trees, enjoying traditional Japanese foods and drinks such as rice cakes (mochi) and sake.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some locations have cherry blossom illuminations, where the trees are lit up at night, creating a magical atmosphere.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Japanese Meteorological Agency provides a forecast of the blooming and peak viewing times for each location.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Cherry Blossom Festival in Japan draws millions of visitors every year.
